body.text: APEC Summit live: Trump, Xi and Putin meet as a trio for first time in China
Submit a comment or question
Live updates
Recap
Here is a summary of today's events:
• Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are meeting for the first time on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen.
• Earlier, Trump conducted bilaterial meetings with both Xi and Putin.
• Trump told Xi he was keen to discuss ending the war in Ukraine during the trilateral.
• And Putin reportedly left his meeting with Trump "in an excellent mood".
• Meanwhile, Prime Minister Anthony Albanese during his APEC speech addressed Putin directly telling him: "End your war, end it now."

Putin: Our three states have 'joint responsibility' for peace
Putin says Russia, China and the US can help make the world more stable if they cooperate constructively.
Speaking through a translator, Putin said: "Our three states have joint responsibility in maintaining peace and security."
He said the three leaders should discuss global and regional issues, as well as energy security.
"Our countries have numerous shared interests in the settlements of regional conflicts, including, obviously, the conflict in Ukraine," he said.
"We focused on that during our bilateral meeting [with Donald Trump].
"We have shared interests in the fight against the threats and challenges of our times — namely, international terrorism, transnational organised crime etc."
Now that's a table
Here's a look inside the room where Trump, Xi and Putin are meeting.
Trump says trilateral meeting 'making history'
Donald Trump has told Xi and Putin that their trilateral is "making history" and that all the problems in the world will be discussed.

He's gone on to say the three countries are "uniquely positioned" to discuss reducing nuclear weapons and that the war in Ukraine will be on the agenda, a subject that had already featured prominently in his conversation with Putin.
Trump has also taken another swipe at the International Criminal Court, calling the tribunal "out of control".
Xi: Positive interaction among major powers is not optional
Xi Jinping is holding the first-ever China-Russia-US summit with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump.
According to China's readout, Xi said: "When major powers get along, the world is at peace. When major powers fight, the world is in chaos."
He said the world is no longer a set of isolated islands, and that major powers bear special responsibilities.
Good relations among them, he said, "is not a multiple-choice question, but a required one."

Xi said China's partnership with Russia and its push for a "constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability" are helping to create major-power relations marked by peaceful coexistence and overall stability.

Xi said the world was "not at peace", so China, Russia and the US — as permanent members of the UN Security Council — should set an example. They should work together on global challenges and help keep the peace.
Xi tells Putin and Trump they should work together
As the trilateral begins, Xi tells Trump and Putin that their three countries have a joint responsibility to maintain peace and security and should work together to address global challenges.
"We will be having discussions on the theme of upholding world peace and promoting strategic stability in major country relations," he said.
"We are a community with a shared future."
Setting the stage
Ahead of the leaders' arrival for the trilateral meeting, staff got to work preparing the venue.
Putin, Xi and Trump meet
We are starting to see images of the meeting between the three leaders.
Trump-Xi-Putin meeting begins
The historic meeting between Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin is underway in Shenzhen.
It's the first official meeting between the three nuclear-armed nations.
We will bring you more as it comes to hand.
Putin arrives for historic meeting
Vladimir Putin has arrived for the meeting with Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, according to Chinese state media sources.
Putin has left for meeting
According to Russian state media, Putin is on his way to the trilateral with Trump and Xi.
A motorcade was seen moving at pace through the streets of Shenzhen.
Big meeting delayed
US media is reporting that the meeting between Xi, Trump and Putin has been delayed.
Sources say Xi and Trump are having lunch together, with the day's schedule now running well behind.
Where is the meeting taking place?
Trump, Xi and Putin will meet at Kylin Villa, a state-owned guesthouse in Shenzhen, set amid hills and water.
Security has been stepped up at the compound, a cluster of standalone villas, ahead of the talks.
The 380,000-square-metre site has hosted China's top leaders and visiting foreign dignitaries, including former North Korean leader Kim Jong Il.
It also has family ties to Xi Jinping. His father, Xi Zhongxun, spent most of his last 12 years in Shenzhen.
"Shenzhen is my home. I want to watch it grow," he once said, according to a local newspaper. In his final months, he went to Kylin Villa to rest.
Xi Zhongxun was one of the main advocates and founders of the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone.
In 1979, he asked China's central government for greater autonomy and proposed setting aside areas in Shenzhen and elsewhere as export processing or trade cooperation zones.
The move helped transform Shenzhen from what is often described as a "small fishing village" and profoundly reshaped China's modern institutional framework.
Trump raises Huang scandal with Xi
Last night, the US president reportedly referred to the scandal surrounding Jensen Huang "just briefly".

"We did not discuss it. I might have referred to it just briefly because it's such a tragedy. It's a tragedy. He's such a brilliant man," Trump said in an interview with Fox News on Thursday, adding that he and Xi had spoken about AI "the whole evening" at dinner.
Huang resigned after revelations about extramarital affairs, including an alleged affair with Alice Huang (no relation), who is alleged to be a Chinese spy
Asked if the affair was a national security threat, Trump said: "I haven't heard that she was a spy."
Reporting with Reuters
Key Event
Two Russian bombers circle Taiwan as China hosts APEC
Taiwan says two Russian Tu-95 military aircraft flew near its eastern airspace on Thursday.
They came in from the south and flew past the island's east.
Then they headed north-east, passing off Keelung.
The timing coincides with the APEC summit.
Taiwan's defence ministry says the aircraft entered its air defence identification zone on Thursday morning.
It says it tracked them the whole way and responded appropriately.
It's not the first time this week.
On Tuesday, Taiwan said two Russian military aircraft had flown south along its east coast.
Minran Liu, from the University of Queensland, said the flights may suggest Russia is trying to "demonstrate its broader military presence and influence in the region".
"The timing is interesting, but there's no public evidence that these flights were coordinated with China or specifically planned around the meeting," Dr Liu said.
Is this the first trilateral meeting of its kind?
This is the first-ever formal trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, China, and Russia.
However, it's not the first time leaders of the three countries have attended the same intergovernmental events.
This trio attended the G20 summits in Hamburg in 2017 and Osaka in 2019, among others.
Xi had meetings separately with Obama and Putin at the 2016 G20 summit.
At the 2019 summit, leaders of China, India and Russia held a trilateral meeting and discussed economic cooperation.
Key Event
Trump on his way to historic meeting
Donald Trump is on his way to the historic meeting with Putin and Xi, with his motorcade making its way through the streets of Shenzhen.
Key Event
Xi to preside over trilateral meeting
Chinese state media outlet CCTV is reporting that Xi Jinping will preside over the first official meeting between the US, China and Russia.
We're waiting for this historic moment to begin. Stick with us.
Reporting with Reuters
In pictures: Albanese at APEC
Key Event
Indonesia aims to expand market access
Indonesia's trade minister, Budi Santoso, says his country's participation in this year's APEC summit presents an "opportunity" to push for "tangible benefits" for all members.
"Including expanding market access and increasing export opportunities for Indonesian products," he said in a statement.
Budi said APEC members remained a primary trading target for Indonesia.
According to official data, Indonesia's total trade with APEC countries last year reached almost $US400 billion.
The Indonesian government also said it wanted to be involved in developing an AI ecosystem among APEC members to ensure the technology was utilised in a "safe, inclusive, and human-centred" manner.
"This provides space for everyone to promote the procurement of safe and responsible artificial intelligence, as well as data centres," said Santo Darmosumarto from Indonesia's Foreign Ministry.
📹: Did Trump fall asleep at leaders' meeting?
The US president has always dismissed any suggestion he's not in peak physical condition.
He's had a busy few days, flying to Manila for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) meeting, where he inked a new trade deal with the Philippines, before flying on to China.
Earlier today, the US president appeared to have a moment of shuteye during the APEC leaders' meeting. You can watch it here.
Analysis: Is the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting a 'Yalta 2.0'?
There's been plenty of speculation about what today's meeting could lead to.

Many analysts have pondered whether it could be a "Yalta 2.0" — a reference to the meeting of Winston Churchill, Franklin D Roosevelt and Joseph Stalin in the city of Yalta towards the end of World War II.
The leaders of the UK, US and the Soviet Union were allies in the fight against Nazi Germany and met to decide the fate of Europe following the war.
But the ABC's Europe Correspondent Kathryn Diss wrote that today's meeting is "probably more about optics than substance".
And each superpower will have its own priorities.

"It offers a photo opportunity for Putin alongside the world's two most powerful leaders. It also places America, historically viewed as the global policeman, in the room with the world's largest authoritarian regimes," she wrote this week.
Russian expert Orysia Lutsevych from London think tank Chatham House described the concept of the meeting as a Yalta 2.0 as "Putin's sick fantasy".
You can read why right here:
Why is the Trump-Xi-Putin meeting significant?

Nick Bisley, a professor of international relations at La Trobe University, said the meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin symbolised a break with the way international diplomacy had been conducted for decades.
Since World War II, the global community has generally embraced the idea of sovereign equality, under which all nation states should be treated equally, he said.
The United Nations and its multilateral framework have been the principal way countries worked through diplomatic differences and security crises.
Professor Bisley said the trilateral meeting "flies in the face" of that tradition and would be "vexing" to countries watching from the sidelines.

"To set something up which tries to present the three countries as the 'Big Three' who will work things out themselves and the rest of us just have to deal with it, presents a pretty galling kind of picture," he said.
Trump says US and China will work to end Ukraine war
We can bring you a little more now from Trump's opening remarks to Xi Jinping ahead of their one-on-one meeting.
"We're looking to both help, with respect to the war in Russia and Ukraine, we'd like to see it ended. I think I can speak for both of us, very much," he said, sitting across from Xi.
"Twenty-five thousand, mostly soldiers, a month are being killed, and President Putin is going to be coming here a little bit later, so we'll have a tri-meeting, trilateral, as they call it.
"We just had a little meeting with President Putin just to set the stage, and I think maybe we'll have a successful meeting."
Chinese state media outlet CCTV is reporting that the pair's meeting has just ended. We will bring you the latest on that once we know more.
Is AI safety on the agenda for Trump and Xi?
Donald Trump and Xi Jinping are meeting today as the United States and China compete for supremacy in artificial intelligence.
While Trump has said he does not want safety regulations to put the US behind in that competition, the two countries have been discussing ways to communicate about AI issues.
In September, they agreed to set up a communication channel for AI incidents, as well as establish a dialogue about the technology's risks and benefits.
Will the leaders revisit the issue during today's trilateral meeting with Vladimir Putin?
Marina Zhang, a researcher in technology and geopolitics at the University of Technology Sydney, said it was more likely a topic for the separate bilateral meeting between Trump and Xi.
However, experts did not anticipate a major treaty or bargain on AI.
"The realistic goal is not a grand US-China AI safety agreement. It is more likely to make the September mechanisms operational," Dr Zhang said.

Kyle Chan, an expert on China's technology development and US-China relations at the Brookings Institution, said there was some hope that both sides could start a regular AI dialogue and an incident notification mechanism.
"Ultimately, given the deep distrust, it's important that regular communication channels are established and kept open," he said.
What is Beijing saying ahead of the trilateral summit?
China's Foreign Ministry has described the meeting as having "groundbreaking significance", a phrase that has also been picked up by state media.
The Global Times says the summit challenges the long-held idea that big powers "inevitably head toward confrontation".
The message Beijing wants to send is that dialogue between major powers is still possible.
But Beijing is also trying to keep expectations in check.

A commentary account affiliated with People's Daily has warned against talk of a "great-power condominium", pushing back against the idea that the three countries are carving up global influence among themselves.
So, what will the leaders actually discuss?
That's been the question on reporters' minds, but the answer from Beijing has remained much the same.
Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun says the leaders will "exchange views in depth on important issues concerning global peace".
In pictures: More from Putin and Trump's pull-aside meeting
Key Event
Albanese tells Putin to end Ukraine war in direct appeal at APEC

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has directly called on Russian President Vladimir Putin to end the war in Ukraine, using an address to world leaders at APEC to warn that global conflicts are driving up inflation and putting pressure on household budgets.
Speaking at the summit in Shenzhen, China, Albanese singled out Putin ahead of his highly anticipated meeting with US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping later today.
"And I say very directly to President Putin: end your war, end it now," Albanese said.
Putin was in the room at the time, and Albanese was looking directly at him as he spoke.
The prime minister said the wars in Ukraine and the Middle East were among the biggest disruptions to global trade, with their economic impacts being felt around the world.
"Military conflict, disrupted global supply chains, and increasing challenges to the international rules that have underpinned decades of growth are impacting our national economies," he said.
"I welcome the meeting being held this afternoon between President Xi, President Trump, and President Putin, and we hope for positive outcomes in the interests of the world."
Albanese also used his address to call for stronger international cooperation on artificial intelligence, warning the rapidly developing technology must remain under human control.
"AI has been created by humans. It must be controlled by humans, and it must benefit humanity," he said.
The prime minister said Australia was developing national standards for AI to ensure the technology was used safely and in the national interest.
He also reaffirmed Australia’s support for free trade, telling leaders that the government had abolished more than 1,000 tariffs since coming to office.
Albanese thanked Xi for hosting the summit and praised his emphasis on free and open trade, noting China accounted for more than a quarter of Australia's exports.
Key Event
Trump's opening remarks to Xi
During his opening remarks, Trump told Xi: "Nobody in any other place can do what we can do."
He said that both he and Xi felt strongly that oil should continue to flow through the Strait of Hormuz.
He also spoke about the tariff war between the US and China, saying the two countries have split tariffs in a "fair way".
He mentioned that he plans to discuss ending the war in Ukraine with Xi and Putin during the trilateral.
In pictures: Trump and Xi in bilateral meeting
Key Event
Xi to Trump: 'I remain committed to working with you'
Xi Jinping and Donald Trump held a bilateral meeting in Shenzhen.
Xi's message was upbeat. He said China-US relations were generally stable and improving.
He also said he was willing to continue working with Trump.
The goal, he said, was to keep the relationship on the right track.
Xi then spoke about building a constructive relationship of strategic stability. He called that effort "unprecedented".
"I remain committed to working with you," he told Trump.
Trump to discuss ending Ukraine war with Putin and Xi
The US president has flagged his intention to discuss ending the Ukraine war with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin later today, Reuters reports.
We'll bring you more on that as it comes to hand.
Key Event
Putin leaves Trump meeting 'in excellent mood', Russian media says
The US and Russian leaders met for just under an hour, according to the White House press pool, which is accredited to cover the president's visit.
Media aren't usually allowed behind closed doors at these meetings, and this was no exception.
But we are starting to get some reactions in state-controlled Russian media.
Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov was quoted by TASS as saying the Ukraine war was the main topic of conversation between the pair.
Bilateral ties and the pair's meeting with Xi Jinping were also reportedly discussed.
Ushakov was also quoted as saying that Putin left the meeting "in an excellent mood".
You can check out Donald Trump's brief statement before the pair met right here.
Reporting with Reuters
What did APEC leaders eat in Shenzhen?
World leaders attending the APEC summit enjoyed a welcome banquet last night.
The menu was mostly Cantonese, with a few international touches.
It started with a cold dish called "Pengcheng", Shenzhen's traditional nickname.
Then came fish maw soup with Chinese green olives, followed by stir-fried lobster with ginger and spring onions.
There was also steamed grouper with soy sauce and steak with mushrooms.
For something lighter, there was baby cabbage with morel mushrooms and chestnuts in a saffron sauce.
Dessert? A trio of Cantonese dim sum: sweet red bean soup with tangerine peel and lotus seeds, plus cake, fruit and ice cream.
For drinks, guests had the option of tea or coffee, or wine from China.
Not a bad way to say welcome to Shenzhen.
Military tensions in Asia loom over meeting of superpowers
As world leaders were descending on Asia for this series of high-stakes meetings, Japan was sending fighter jets into the skies as two suspected Russian military planes entered its airspace.
Tokyo has lodged a "strong protest" with the Kremlin after the incident in the early hours of Tuesday morning, with a government spokesperson describing it as a threat to the country's security.
South Korea also sent up fighter jets, and Taiwan described the Russian flights as a "threat to the peaceful and stable status quo in the Asia-Pacific region".
Analysts say the military deployment is a way for Russia to send a message about its reach and relationships in Asia ahead of the meeting between Putin, Trump and Xi.
Their meeting will be closely watched in Japan and South Korea, which are close allies of the United States and are encircled by China, Russia, and North Korea.

On the sidelines of ASEAN this week, Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi Sanae and South Korean President Lee Jae Myung spoke about "deepening" their own cooperation, against a backdrop of increasing tension surrounding Taiwan, tightening bonds between North Korea and Russia, and concerns about the reliability of their biggest security partner, the US.
PM criticised for photo with Putin
Greens leader David Shoebridge has criticised Anthony Albanese for standing in the traditional APEC "family photo" alongside invited world leaders, including Vladimir Putin.
Albanese said before APEC he would respect the wishes of the host country, China, but would also reiterate Australia's opposition to Russia's war in Ukraine.
Shoebridge called on the PM to put more sanctions on Russia's economy and stop its oil from reaching Australian shores.
"Instead, he is travelling round the world getting photos with the bloke," he said on his way into parliament this morning.
Acting PM Richard Marles has rejected any suggestion that the photo indicates Australia is softening its stance on Russia.

"When you go to these meetings, you pay respect to the host country, you participate in the family photo. That's what has happened here. We've done that. Our prime minister has done that, along with other world leaders who are in exactly the same position as Australia," Marles said.
"That photo does not for a moment change our position in respect of the war in Ukraine."
Key Event
Trump and Xi begin bilateral meeting
Trump and Xi have started their bilateral meeting.
Key Event
Trump is having a moment in Shenzhen
#Trump enjoys Shenzhen's night view and #Trump thanks China are trending on Chinese social media Weibo.
A short video clip of US President Donald Trump waving through the rear passenger window of a limousine after he arrived in China has been trending on Chinese social media.
The video caption says Trump didn't close the curtain because he enjoyed the city's night views.
"It looks like [he is] falling in love with China," a Weibo user commented under the video.
"Shenzhen is too beautiful," said another post.
Another video of Trump saying he appreciated China's big welcoming ceremony was also trending on social media.
"And not only that, the fanfare, the beauty, the pageantry, the thousands of people, the young children, the soldiers, the whole thing," Trump told Fox News in an interview.
"It was great respect, and I appreciate that. That's a big win for us. It's a big win for China too."
Reporting with Reuters
Analysis: AI and the Huang affair hangs over Trump-Xi meeting

When Donald Trump and Xi Jinping sit down for their meeting in Shenzhen, there's one subject neither will want to talk about: the alleged Chinese spying operation against recently resigned Nvidia chief Jensen Huang.
Ironically, AI is probably the issue the two most need to talk about.
The US and China will largely define how rapidly AI develops and develops in a way that minimises potential damage from "rogue agents".
They may talk about AI generally, but the real test of their preparedness to discuss the issue was shown when Xi visited Washington, and the two avoided coming up with any clear guidelines for AI.
The reality is both men, and both countries, are too competitive to want to give up any option that may be curbed by the other.
It's generally believed the US is leading the AI "race" — thanks largely to super chip giant Nvidia — and that China is six months behind.
Which is where the so-called spy scandal comes in. Reportedly, US intelligence believes Alice Huang (no relation) was working for China when she developed a relationship with Huang.
The US version is that Ms Huang used a company in Singapore — Megaspeed — to buy Nvidia chips using her "special relationship" with Mr Huang.
Trump says he's not even sure that Ms Huang was a spy. He's said that often attractive Chinese women are stereotyped as spies.
It is difficult to predict what Trump may do, but based on past meetings with Xi and other world leaders, he's shown a pattern of avoiding conflict.
The stories are legion of how he's confronted world leaders on the phone. His phone conversation with former prime minister Malcolm Turnbull was a major story.
But generally — with an exception for Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy — Trump prefers not to confront world leaders in public.
He particularly wants a warm relationship with Xi.

It may change, but for the moment the general view in Washington is that Trump wants a meeting with the Chinese leader, accompanied by a warm photo-opportunity, rather than conflict on any issue, particularly allegations about an alleged Chinese spy.
Shenzhen shows off
China is keen to present Shenzhen at its best to world leaders this week, and there are some noticeable changes in the megacity.
Drones, which regularly deliver food in parts of the city, have been grounded by operator Meituan for 10 days.
More than 1.5 million local car owners have pledged to stay off the roads in exchange for APEC car stickers.
They have been promised transit cards worth up to 100 yuan ($22) if they keep their word.
The city has long restricted horn use, but this month motorists have been banned from unnecessary beeping, with acoustic cameras enforcing the new rule.
Motorists caught using the horn excessively risk fines starting at 300 yuan ($66).
Local police have banned cars with out-of-town plates from most city districts.
E-bike riders will get a discount on their insurance if they dismount, while parked bikes are being removed from main streets.
Areas near the summit venue have also been spruced up with garden beds and newly paved roads.
Reporting with Reuters
Xi says China is 'rooted in the Asia Pacific'
In his keynote address earlier today, Xi Jinping announced that China would contribute $US20 million ($29.9 million) "to support APEC's practical cooperation".
He also said China was "rooted in the Asia Pacific".
You can hear part of his speech, which details where the $US20 million will go, right here.
📷 In pictures: Trump, Xi and Putin pose for 'family photo' with other leaders
Who's attending APEC?
Apart from Trump, Xi and Putin, several other familiar faces are at the summit.
Japan's Sanae Takaichi is on her first official visit to China as prime minister.
Taiwan, which takes part in APEC as Chinese Taipei, sent Acer founder Stan Shih as its representative, instead of a political leader.
Taiwan's participation has been a sensitive issue with China because it views the democratically governed island as its own territory.
Business heavyweights have also been invited. A total of 115 Fortune Global 500 companies have sent executives, according to Chinese state media.
US firms make up almost 20 per cent, the biggest share after China. Elon Musk is also attending.
Chinese companies include Xiaomi, BYD, CATL, Baidu and Unitree Robotics. International names include Google, Boeing, Rio Tinto, Mastercard, Visa, Citigroup, HSBC and UPS.
There is also one notable no-show. Nvidia's Jensen Huang was expected to travel with Trump but pulled out after resigning as CEO last week.
Key Event
Trump meets with Putin
Donald Trump has greeted Vladimir Putin with a warm handshake on the sidelines of the summit.

"We've had a great relationship for many years. We know each other for a long time, and I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start. But I think they'll come out of this," Trump told Putin.
He then flagged the pair would have a second meeting later on today, but didn't go into further details.
Earlier today, Trump spoke at APEC's plenary session, which all leaders attend.
He said that AI is "almost completely good", not wavering from his view that the technology should face minimal regulation.
The US president also described America as a "Pacific power for hundreds of years, and we continue to work to promote growth and stability, sovereignty, prosperity and peace throughout this region".
Analysis: Trump and Xi's airport hug
It did look remarkably chummy and caught a lot of China watchers by surprise, but I don't think we should assume this means the pair are now best buds.
To be clear, this was an extraordinary meeting on the tarmac in Shenzhen.

It's the first time Xi Jinping has personally greeted a visiting head of state at an airport, let alone welcomed them with an embrace — the kind of greeting usually reserved for his close ally, Russian President Vladimir Putin.

But to put this in context, China is a proud nation that values tradition and reciprocity. Just a few months ago, Trump bestowed the same honour of a personal greeting on Xi when he visited the US. So it's not a stretch to see why China wouldn't want to be outdone and would want to match that level of hospitality.
But don't be fooled by the warm atmosphere; this is a relationship fraught with delicate and wide disagreements, including on issues like trade, AI and tech, and Taiwan.
What we can read into this airport embrace is that both parties want today's bilateral, as well as the trilateral meeting with Putin, to go well, at least from an optics perspective.
And it does appear the personal relationship between Trump and Xi is growing closer, something both leaders want despite their vast differences.
Another meeting could be more important than Trump-Xi-Putin
While the bilateral meeting between Xi and Trump seems to be an afterthought, for many, it could actually be more important than the trilateral meeting involving Putin.

"I think the trilateral meeting will be a lot of pomp and photographs, but not much outcome, whereas the US-China one could actually be significant," said Nick Bisley, a professor of international relations at La Trobe University.

He said the bilateral meeting — the third between Xi and Trump this year, with one more expected next month — could touch on key topics such as Taiwan and artificial intelligence, and even former Nvidia chief Jensen Huang.

Professor Bisley said his guess was that because the landscape was so unsettled, the outcome would likely just be an anodyne statement about AI being an important technology that needs to be regulated.

"But what's the tone and tenor of that relationship? Can the stability of the relationship that was established earlier be continued? Does it get frosty? Does Trump revert to his more hawkish position on China? And that's all a bit up for grabs," he said.

"You can overrate how important these bilateral meetings are, but both the US and China have highly personalised political systems at the moment, so seeing how those two get along and what they achieve or not will be pretty important to watch."
Shenzhen, China's Silicon Valley
The metropolis of about 18 million people is just north of Hong Kong and is known for its development of AI, driverless cars and robotics.
It's commonly referred to as China's Silicon Valley.
Huawei, EV maker BYD, internet and gaming giant Tencent and electronics manufacturer Oppo are some of the major companies headquartered in Shenzhen.
Drones are also regularly used to deliver food in parts of the city, which has increasingly attracted young entrepreneurs.
Shenzhen was largely a rural area before it made history in 1980, when then-leader Deng Xiaoping declared it China's first special economic zone.
This opened the door to foreign direct investment and private enterprises. The city then evolved from a low-cost manufacturing hub to a global hardware and technology innovation powerhouse.

"Shenzhen is one of the most important symbols of China’s reform and opening up through its strong global role in trade, manufacturing, and innovation," Gary Ng, senior economist for Asia Pacific at French bank Natixis told AP.
APEC in a nutshell
APEC stands for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation.
It was an idea born in Australia.
Then-prime minister Bob Hawke proposed the idea in 1989, and the first meeting was held in Canberra in November that year.
It began small.
There were just 12 members, including Australia, the US, Japan and South Korea. China, Hong Kong and Taiwan joined in 1991, and the group now has 21 members.
Why the word 'economies'?
APEC does not call its members "countries" because the test for joining is being a separate economy rather than a state. That is how Beijing, Hong Kong and Taiwan can sit at the same table.
Leaders took a while to show up.
The early meetings were for ministers only, and the first leaders' meeting was held in Seattle in 1993.
Nothing is legally binding.
APEC runs on consensus and voluntary action, so it is more of a "talk until we agree" club than a rule-making body.
The 'family photo' is a tradition.
Leaders pose in outfits that nod to the host country, and fans look forward to it every year.
Sydney had a moment in 2007.
Comedy group The Chaser drove a fake motorcade into the restricted zone, which some critics described as a security failure.
Now it is China's turn again.
This year's summit in Shenzhen is the third time China has hosted, after the summits in Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014.
A historic meeting ahead
Hi everyone, and welcome to our live blog of the much-anticipated meeting of the leaders of the three major nuclear powers: the US, China and Russia.
The meeting is taking place on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen.
We're also expecting a couple of important bilateral meetings, including one between US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
